cells.rule: §28.3: "every already-produced, not-yet-consumed unbound owned temporary is disposed during unwinding by the same implicit `try`/`finally` mechanism as named locals" | §28.3: "a temporary whose producing subexpression never ran was never produced" | §28.7: "a throwing disposer during overwrite propagates after the store is abandoned, leaving the new value an unbound owned temporary disposed by [§28.3](#sec-unbound-owned-temporaries)'s unbound-temporary rule — on this exception edge, during the unwind" | §35.5: "An exception out of an arm disposes the not-yet-consumed remainder during unwinding ([K3.15](#sec-kernel-k3))." | §30.9: "a task disposed while its own fault exception is in flight defers that disposal until the exception's handling completes"

Each produced, untransferred temporary is disposed once during the unwind; one transferred into an `owned` parameter is the callee's; the abandoned-store RHS and an owning match's remainder are temporaries of this pass. No escape.

cells.rule: K9: "never by any scope's end, and no scope-end machinery ever touches it" | §28.8.1: "An exception raised while evaluating the receiver, the index or the replacement, or by one of those checks — an out-of-range index, a `KeyNotFoundException` at an absent dictionary key, `NullReferenceException` under `!` at a location holding `null`, a throwing constructor in `e` — leaves the location unchanged" | K9.5: "drop-on-overwrite (K3.11) is RHS-first, so a throwing RHS leaves the slot untouched and still-owned" | §28.4: "the remaining owned-field disposals (reverse declaration order) and the base-class chain complete, and physical reclamation still occurs"

cells.note: A field is never discharged by an unwind; it holds a live value (or `null`) at every instant, so no exception edge can leave it vacated. A raise in the replacing `move`'s receiver, index, replacement or check leaves the location unchanged and the produced replacement is an unbound temporary the unwind disposes; a throwing RHS of an overwrite leaves the field owned; a throwing destructor completes the remaining field disposals. The v0.334 straight-line window, its `finally` exclusion and the vacated state are retired (0174). Hunted: a scope-end disposal that raises after a take (the field already holds its replacement); a `move` inside a `try` with the restoration-free `catch` (nothing to restore).

cells.rule: §28.8.1: "a replacement already produced is an unbound owned temporary disposed by the unwind" | §28.8.1: "If the call then raises — from the callee's body, or from a constructor's field initializers or body ([§22.9](#sec-owned-fields-and-exception-safety)) — the caller's binding is moved-from on the exception edge exactly as on the normal one" | §28.4: "an owning collection's element cascade and its `Clear()`" | §29.2: "On *exception* edges — whether from an explicit `throw` or from a method call that propagates an exception out of the body — the iteration variable is auto-disposed"

The v0.334 straight-line slot window and its body-local collection exception are retired (0174). No escape.

cells.note: Unchanged in verdict: an owning-match arm's transferred binding is an owned local of the arm (exception-path discharge), the remainder is disposed in the unwind, a throwing guard transfers nothing; move-only locals unwind slot by slot under §28.4. The v0.334 inline-array slot window is retired (0174): a slot exchange leaves `null` or the replacement, and a raise inside it leaves the slot unchanged. No escape.

No escape.

cells.rule: §29.7: "A **body fault** reaches the same state by the same pass: an exception that escapes the body out of `MoveNext()` (or faults the task a `MoveNextAsync()` returned) is the frame's **completion**" | §29.7: "the machine is completed before the exception reaches the consumer; a later `MoveNext()` returns `false`" | §29.8: "a body fault being a completion ([§29.7](#sec-disposal-of-partially-consumed-iterators)), the parameter then disposed in that unwind before the exception reaches the consumer" | §30.1: "on every completion path (success, fault, and cancellation), after the body's `using var` cleanups and `finally` clauses"

A later `MoveNext()` returns `false`; the consumer's eventual `Dispose()` finds nothing pending. Async frames fault their task and tear down at that terminal state. No escape.

The v0.333 form-(iv) face (a static slot moved inside a window an exception crosses) is gone with the form (K9.4 bars any `move` of static storage). Static initialization failure is C4's; a throwing static disposer is C12's.

Re-hunted at v0.334: `new Holder(x, move x)` is now rejected at the `move` (#5750 ruling, a live borrow at the consume), and an uncaptured primary parameter is named in §28.3's order sentence. Unbound temporaries join the same stack at their production."

A `using var` (and the compiler-introduced slots) in a constructor body is disposed on the construction-unwind edge as on every exit edge; §28.10's new parenthetical (process termination unwinds nothing, #5779) is not a construction edge. The only thing the text lets leak is a raw resource held in no owned field, §28.4's recorded one-resource-per-wrapper discipline (no K1 obligation). No escape.

Temporaries produced in a `new` argument list, a field initializer or a constructor body are unwound in reverse production order; one already transferred into an `owned` constructor parameter is the callee's. The v0.334 side note is closed: K8's enumerated full-expression positions now name a constructor's `base(…)`/`this(…)` chaining clause (#5844). §28.8.1's sentence now also names a `move` result among the already-produced temporaries (quoted around the inserted parenthetical).

cells.rule: §22.9: "When construction throws, the compiler unwinds the partially-constructed instance in **reverse declaration order** within the derived class" | §22.9: "Owned fields assigned imperatively in the body are also disposed if assigned successfully before the throwing statement." | §28.4: "**The destructor body runs on disposal, never on construction unwind — hold one raw resource per owning wrapper.**" | §28.8.1: "a `move x.f` before the field's first assignment is a definite-assignment violation" | §28.8.1: "After the first assignment, the replacing `move` is admitted as in any other body." | §28.2: "the cascade over an explicitly disposed field, a drop-on-overwrite over an explicitly disposed value, the exit pass — reads a live flag in both modes"
cells.cite: §22.8, §22.9, §22.10, §28.2 (The compiler-inserted free), §28.4, §28.8.1 (*Constructors and destructors*), K9.2, K9.3; proposal 0174
cells.note: Every owned field whose initialization completed is disposed once on each construction-throw edge, captures first, then the base subobject's `Dispose()`. A constructor body's `move` is barred before first assignment (definite assignment) and is the replacing `move` after it, so the field holds its replacement when a later statement throws and the unwind disposes that replacement once, while the taken value is a local the exception-path discharge disposes. The v0.334 vacated-field face is retired (0174). A constructor body's explicit `_r.Dispose()` before a throw: the unwind's `Dispose()` reads a live flag (no-op). No escape.

cells.rule: §28.11: "Disposal of the collection itself — at the end of a `using var` scope, in a destructor's auto-dispose pass, or at static-program-exit for a `static owned` field — disposes every element it still holds, then frees the backing storage" | §22.9: "An exception in the **constructor body** (step 3) triggers disposal of every owned field assigned during initialization (step 2) and the base subobject. Owned fields assigned imperatively in the body are also disposed if assigned successfully before the throwing statement." | K3.15: "**Edge parity.** The exception edge performs the same implicit disposal as the normal edge, on the single establishment-ordered cleanup stack; the only difference is the lint. Unbound temporaries join the same stack at their production."
cells.cite: §28.11 (Owning collections), §22.9, §28.3 (Unbound owned temporaries), K3.15
cells.note: An owning collection held in an owned field is disposed by §22.9's unwind and cascades over its elements; one held in a constructor local or temporary is disposed by the exception-path discharge. Elements produced for a literal or an `Add` whose evaluation is cut short by a throw are unbound temporaries (disposed by the unwind) until they are taken by the collection, after which the collection's cascade owns them. No escape found. Re-checked at v0.334: `Clear()` is now a named multi-value pass; nothing on this path moved.

cells.cite: §22.9, §28.4 step 2, §28.5 (*Generic class fields*), §15.3 (Field placement), §15.1.1, §35.4, §28.9; #5789, #5799, #5890 (closed rulings)

Re-hunted: a generic `Box<T>` with `owned _slot: T` at an owning-choice substitution whose constructor throws after the store (per instantiation: disposed by the unwind).

cells.rule: §31.1: "ownership transfers to the runtime's exception machinery, which disposes the exception after the matching catch arm completes" | §22.9: "a disposer that throws during it **supersedes** that exception under [§28.4](#sec-the-destructor)'s rule, and the superseded exception is recorded into the superseding one's `SupersededChain` before the drop" | §22.7: "the original exception never propagates raw out of static initialization; it is observable only as `InnerException`." | §31.4: "**The cached `TypeInitializationException` and its `InnerException` are runtime-owned for the life of the process**" | §30.5: "The task's own block stays live until that terminal state"
cells.cite: §31.1 (Exception ownership), §22.9, §28.4, §31.2, §22.7, §31.4, §30.5 (Disposing an unsettled task), #5788 (closed)
cells.note: Sub-shapes: (1) the in-flight construction exception is the runtime's, disposed once after its catch arm, or superseded during the unwind and then disposed once after its snapshot is recorded: once. (2) A static initializer's escaping exception becomes the cached `TypeInitializationException`'s `InnerException`, and both are runtime-owned for the process and exempt from dispose-after-arm, which is what makes every later re-raise sound: exempt. (3) Supersession of the cached instance drops it undisposed (§31.2). Hunted: re-raising the cached TIE on every touch after a catch arm completed (exempt by name, so no double dispose). No escape. New sub-shape checked at v0.334: an unsettled task held in an owned field of an object whose construction throws is disposed by §22.9's unwind under §30.5's new unsettled-task rule (proposal 0168): the frame's late delivery is disposed by the attached continuation and the task's block stays live until its terminal state. Once.

cells.rule: §29.8: "An iterator method may take `owned` parameters. The call transfers the argument into the frame it mints" | §30.1: "An async method's `owned` parameters transfer into the state-machine frame at call time, exactly as an iterator's do" | §31.4: "Allocation failure is not an exception. There is no `OutOfMemoryException`; nothing is catchable; no unwinding runs"
cells.note: Unchanged. No constructor is a deferred activation; a frame is minted by its call, which runs no user code before its `owned` arguments are frame-held, and its only failure is allocation failure, which unwinds nothing. Proposal 0167's single-consumption iterable changes who disposes the parameters later (C11), not construction.

cells.rule: §22.13: "A static `owned` field whose initializer threw is not disposed (its value was never produced). A static `owned` field on a type left in a failed state ([§22.7](#sec-constructors)) whose initializer *did* complete successfully before the failing initializer is disposed normally." | §22.13: "the pass drains until no initialized-but-undisposed static `owned` field remains" | §22.13: "A static field of owning-inline-array type whose initializer threw is not disposed (the array's slots were never observable)" | §22.13: "A `static readonly` field of class type or interface type that is not marked `owned` is exempt from the [§28.8](#sec-ownership-transfer) ownership-discharge requirement" | §22.7: "The runtime makes no guarantee about ordering of disposal across types when one of the types is in a failed state."
cells.cite: §22.7 (failed state), §22.12 rule 1, §22.13 (cycle backstop; Disposal of static owned fields; exemption), §31.4, K3.15
cells.note: `static owned` fields and the one admitted static owning inline array (`static readonly`, §22.12 note (h); form (iv) retired at v0.334) whose value was produced are disposed once at exit even when their type is left failed; a field whose initializer threw holds nothing; non-`owned` statics are exempt. Unchanged otherwise: a field assigned in the static constructor body is enrolled through the drain's 'initialized-but-undisposed' wording, and the cross-type exit order among failed types is explicitly unspecified (order only).

cells.rule: K1.6: "Values of runtime-managed type (`string`, `Type`, boxed value types, function values) and of ordinary value type carry no classification and no obligation" | §28.9: "a closure cannot extend the lifetime of an owned class instance, so reclaiming the closure never leaves a destructor un-run."
cells.cite: K1.6, §28.1 clauses 2–3, §28.9, §8.6, §35.8 (owning choices cannot be boxed)
cells.note: Strings, `Type`, boxes and function values in fields, initializers or constructor locals carry no obligation to unwind. Hunted for an exemption leak: a closure built in a constructor over an owned local (a capture is a borrow, §28.9; a plain function-typed primary parameter cannot be captured into a field, §22.10), and a boxed owning choice (not admitted, §35.8). No obligation-bearing value hides behind the exemption on this path.

cells.rule: §28.3: "A **moved-from** LHS is an owned-state LHS holding no live value: it requires an owned RHS and displaces nothing" | §28.3: "An **explicitly-disposed** LHS requires an owned RHS too and displaces a **logically disposed** value: the store is that value's release point" | §28.3: "so the overwrite runs no user code and is non-throwable, exactly as the scope end of an explicitly-disposed binding frees it without disposing it again" | §28.7: "The right-hand side is evaluated first; then, if the previous value is live (non-null — and, for a binding, not moved-from), it is disposed; then the new value is stored." | §28.7: "an explicitly-disposed owned local that is reassigned takes the same free at the store"
cells.cite: §28.3 (State match on reassignment), §28.2 (The compiler-inserted free), §28.7, K1 states 3–4, K3.9, K3.11, K4.1, K5.2, K7.4; #5832 (closed, ruling option (a)), #5768; #5830, #5810 (impl)

An explicitly-disposed LHS now displaces a logically disposed value and the store is its release point (the no-op `Dispose()` then the free), so `c.Dispose(); c := new Res();` reclaims the old block at the store, once; a moved-from LHS displaces nothing. The same reading reaches a frame-resident local (R8) and a discarded move-only local (R6, §15.3's per-slot pass). Open route found by this run: an overwrite whose displaced disposer throws, caught inside the local's scope, leaves the binding's content unstated (route R1, R4–R6/C6·abandoned-overwrite).

cells.rule: A5: "`using var` is a scope pin: non-reassignable, never movable out" | §28.10: "`using var` is a scope pin (axiom [A5](#sec-axiom-register)): it is implicitly non-reassignable, and reassigning a `using var` variable is a compile error." | §28.3: "establishing a hidden, unnameable `using var` slot"

cells.rule: §28.7: "a throwing disposer during overwrite propagates after the store is abandoned, leaving the new value an unbound owned temporary disposed by [§28.3](#sec-unbound-owned-temporaries)'s unbound-temporary rule — on this exception edge, during the unwind." | §28.3: "A temporary that is instead bound (to a `var`/`using var`), `move`d, returned, or transferred into an owning location is governed by the corresponding transfer or discharge rule and is **not** disposed under this rule (it would otherwise be disposed twice)."

A binding-atom binding cannot be reassigned inside its single-expression body. No escape found.

cells.rule: §28.7: "The right-hand side is evaluated first; then, if the previous value is live (non-null — and, for a binding, not moved-from), it is disposed; then the new value is stored." | §28.7: "the replacing `move` ([§28.8.1](#sec-the-replacing-move)) is not an overwrite at all: its exchange displaces nothing that is disposed" | §28.7: "a borrow of the displaced value is invalidated at the overwrite, caught as `DisposedAccessException` in checked disposal mode and undefined unchecked" | §28.7: "the store is the disposed block's release point, where [§28.2](#sec-checked-disposal)'s compiler-inserted free reclaims it"

The v0.334 vacated-state face (a store into a field inside its restoration window) is gone: a field always holds a value or `null`, so every store is an ordinary overwrite. Ordinary overwrite incl. `set(owned)` (route): once-backstopped. Open route found by this run: an overwrite whose displaced disposer throws abandons the store at the displaced value's release point, and no text says what the field then holds (route R1, R4–R6/C6·abandoned-overwrite).

cells.rule: §28.11: "takes `owned`; indexer-set disposes the previous value first" | §28.11: "The indexer-set disposes the displaced value per [§28.7](#sec-reassigning-owned-fields)'s drop-on-overwrite ([K3.11](#sec-kernel-k3)) — no explicit `Dispose()` at the assignment site." | §28.11: "An element-level write — an indexer-set — does not draw this warning" | §28.7: "a borrow of the displaced value is invalidated at the overwrite, caught as `DisposedAccessException` in checked disposal mode and undefined unchecked"
cells.cite: §28.11 (slot policy; Owning collections; *`move` on a collection slot*), §23.3, §28.7, K3.11, K5.6, K4.1, stdlib §4.5, §4.9, §4.14; proposal 0174; route R5/C6·reindex (closed)
cells.note: The owning indexer-set disposes the displaced element once (no slot is ever vacated, so no skip case remains); an element borrow of the displaced value meets the K4.1 flag; a throwing displaced disposer is discharged inside the setter. The v0.334 reindex route (a structural mutation relocating a vacated slot) is closed by construction (0174). Open route found by this run: an indexer-set whose displaced element's disposer throws (the stdlib setter is `_storage[i] := value`) leaves the slot's content after the abandoned store unstated (route R1, R4–R6/C6·abandoned-overwrite).

cells.rule: §15.1.1: "A fifth, for one slot, is a **slot store** `arr[i] := e` into a local's or instance field's array: the displaced slot, if live, is disposed before the store" | §15.3: "then each slot of the displaced value that is **live** — non-null, §28.7's liveness test — is disposed, **in reverse slot order**; then the new value is stored." | §15.3: "A slot whose object was logically disposed earlier — by a discard of the value ([§17.13](#sec-the-discard-_)) or an explicit `Dispose()` of the slot ([§28.6](#sec-who-may-dispose)) — is live by that test" | §35.9: "`null` assignment into an owned-state `C?` location is drop-on-overwrite"

cells.rule: K3.3: "an `owned` argument ([§22.3](#sec-parameter-modifiers)) | `move x` at the call site | **moved-from** | frozen (K5.1) | none here — the callee's" | §28.8.1: "The transfer of an `owned` argument completes when the call is **entered**" | K3.13: "An **unmarked read of a class-typed binding never consumes**" | §28.3: "A borrow of the consumed binding passed as an argument or operand evaluated **before** a consuming argument of the same call ([§22.5](#sec-optional-parameters-and-named-arguments)'s textual order) is such a borrow, its use being the call itself" | §28.3: "`Sink(x, move x)` and `Sink(x.Child(), move x)` are rejected at the `move`" | K5.5: "an argument or operand of the same full expression evaluated before the consume and used by its call or operator"
cells.cite: K3 table (K3.1–K3.4, K3.7), K3.13, K5, K5.5, §22.3, §22.4, §22.5, §28.3 (Move semantics; *The consume-site freeze*), §28.8.1 (raise from the consuming call), App. C.3; #5750 (closed, ruling reading 1), #5811 (impl tracker), #5813 (impl-ahead mirror)
cells.note: Every marked transfer of an owned local or `owned` parameter of a synchronous body leaves it moved-from. The new holder discharges, the scope-end and unwind passes skip the binding, and a raise after entry stays with the callee (§28.8.1). An unmarked read only borrows. `out owned` delivers only on normal return. The v0.333 opening is closed by the #5750 ruling: a borrow of the consumed binding passed as an earlier argument or operand is live at the consume, so `Sink(x, move x)` and `Sink(x.Child(), move x)` are rejected. A value-typed read (`Add(x.Id, move x)`) is unaffected. Hunted and closed: `M(move x, x.F())` (the second operand reads a moved-from binding); a named argument written after the move (`Sink(c: move x, view: x)`; §22.5 textual order makes it a moved-from read); `Sink(x.AsSpan(), move x)` (a span holds borrows of `x`); `x.Absorb(move x)` (the receiver is an operand evaluated before the consume and used by the call, K5.5 clause 5); a closure argument over `x` (a live closure). `new T(move n, n)` is #5813's impl-ahead delta, not a spec gap.

cells.note: Unchanged. Each condition or guard evaluation is its own boundary and each body statement its own full expression, so no temporary crosses a back edge. A fresh `for` source is bound once by `__source` and disposed at loop exit. A borrow of a temporary cannot be carried around a loop (K8.4).

cells.rule: K9.1: "the only owned read of an owned field or an owning slot is the **replacing `move`** ([§28.8.1](#sec-the-replacing-move)): `move x.f with e` — and `move coll[i] with e` — stores the owned value `e` into the location and yields the displaced value, owned, in one step with no intermediate state" | §28.8.1: "Where it is not, the clause is **required**; its absence is a compile error naming the two remedies" | §28.8.1: "The replacement `e` is an owned value for the location's declared type: a fresh producer, a `move` result, a named owned binding" | §28.8.1: "a consume of the holder binding inside `e` is frozen as at a call's receiver" | K9.3: "a destructor body may take a field of the object it tears down bare — `move x.f` with no replacement, whatever the field's nullability" | K9: "A field's obligation belongs to the object: it is discharged by the destructor cascade (owned fields, reverse declaration order) or by drop-on-overwrite, never by any scope's end"
cells.cite: K3.1, K4.1, K5.6, K9.1–K9.5, §23.3 (`set(owned)`), §28.5, §28.6, §28.7, §28.8.1 (*The replacing `move`*; *Constructors and destructors*), §9.5 (tie-break); proposal 0174 (#5923); #5695 ruling; routes R4/C5·dtor-bare-take (#5913), R4–R6/C5·exchange
cells.note: Sub-shapes: the replacing `move x.f with e` exchanges in one step, the taker owning the old value and the field the replacement (once); a bare `move x.f` at a nullable field stores `null` (once); a bare take of a non-nullable field outside a destructor is a compile error naming the remedies (rejected). The v0.334 restoration window, vacated state and holder rules are retired: no location is ever empty, so no callee, alias or continuation can meet a hole, and a borrow of the displaced value has the overwrite posture (K5.6, K4.1). Hunted: a holder consumed or rebound inside `e` (frozen); `move b.f with fresh` through a borrowed receiver (admitted, #5695: the overwrite posture); two parameters aliasing one object (each exchange reads the location at its own exchange). Open residue: a destructor's bare take of a non-nullable field read later through another spelling (route R4/C5·dtor-bare-take, #5913).

cells.rule: K9: "no scope-end machinery ever touches it" | K9.2: "so no path carries a restoration obligation, no code can observe a location between a take and a store" | §28.8.1: "the `move` may sit anywhere in a body, before or after a call, across an `await`, inside a `try`"
cells.note: A field is object state, so no join merges its obligation, and under 0174 no per-path restoration is owed after a take: a `move _f with e` in one branch leaves the field holding `e` on that path and untouched on the other. An arm that reads a field is a borrow arm; an arm `move _f with e` is a fresh-producer arm. No escape.

cells.rule: K9.5: "drop-on-overwrite (K3.11) is RHS-first, so a throwing RHS leaves the slot untouched and still-owned" | K9.2: "so no path carries a restoration obligation, no code can observe a location between a take and a store" | §28.7: "The right-hand side is evaluated first; then, if the previous value is live (non-null — and, for a binding, not moved-from), it is disposed; then the new value is stored."
cells.note: Reassigning an owned field inside a loop drops the displaced value each iteration (RHS-first); a replacing `move` per iteration exchanges in one step, the taken value a per-iteration local. The v0.334 loop legs (a field moved before a loop and restored only inside it, rejected; a throwable loop condition inside a window) have no subject under 0174 — the verdict moves from conditional to once. No escape.

cells.rule: §28.11: "`move coll[i] with e` is the replacing `move` at an owning slot: it stores `e` into the i-th slot and yields the slot's previous element, owned, in one step" | §28.11: "the replacement is **required** — `move xs[i] with fresh`, `move d[k] with fresh` — and `move d[k] with fresh` at an absent key raises `KeyNotFoundException` and inserts nothing" | §28.11: "The index is any expression, evaluated once before the exchange, and the receiver is any expression naming an owning slot's holder" | §28.11: "The exchange displaces nothing that is disposed: the indexer-set's drop-on-overwrite ([§28.7](#sec-reassigning-owned-fields)) does not run" | §28.11: "A `Pop`-family member removes the element and returns it as `owned` in a single step, closing the slot" | §28.11: "except through a `static readonly` field, whose slots are fixed"

Ingress takes `owned`, the indexer-set drops the displaced element, `Pop*`/`Drain` hand ownership out, and `move coll[i] with e` exchanges in one step (once); at an `OwningArray<T>`/`OwningDictionary<K, V>` slot the bare take is a compile error naming `PopAt`/`PopValue` (rejected), and at an `OwningBuffer<T>`/`Span<T>`/`[N owned]T?` slot it stores `null` (once). v0.334's two faces are gone with the window: `Clear()` is no restoration of anything (nothing is vacated), and a captured or closure-written index is just an index expression evaluated once, the bounds check running after `e`. Hunted: `move xs[k] with Refill(xs)` where the call grows or shrinks `xs` (checks after `e`, so an out-of-range `k` raises and stores nothing); a slot of a `static owned readonly OwningArray<T>` exchanged (admitted: an element of a static's referent, rule 4's confinement obligation, not K9.4).

cells.rule: K9.2: "so no path carries a restoration obligation, no code can observe a location between a take and a store" | §28.11: "the dominating-kill shape of [§28.2](#sec-checked-disposal)'s use-after-dispose warning, with the kill on the collection rather than on the binding" | §28.11: "A borrow re-taken after the mutation is clean, and a use before the mutation, or on a path the kill does not dominate, draws nothing."
cells.cite: K9.2, K7, K4.1, §28.11, §28.3 (Producers: indexer row); proposal 0174
cells.note: A slot exchanged in one branch owes nothing on any path (0174). An element borrow joined across a conditional `Clear()`/`RemoveAt` is not warned (the kill does not dominate) and falls to K4.1's flag. An arm `move coll[i] with e` is a fresh-producer arm. No escape.

cells.rule: §28.11: "The index is any expression, evaluated once before the exchange" | K9.2: "so no path carries a restoration obligation, no code can observe a location between a take and a store" | §28.11: "partial iteration drains only the elements yielded, and the rest remain"
cells.cite: K9.2, §28.11 (*`move` on a collection slot*), §28.8.1, §29.2, §29.12, stdlib §4.5 (`PopAt`); proposal 0174 (#5923)
cells.note: A loop of `move pool[k] with Make()` exchanges each slot in one step whatever `k` does between iterations (any index expression, checked after `e`); a `for` over `Drain()` takes elements out one per iteration; the per-iteration taken value is a local discharged on the back edge. The v0.334 index-stability and window legs have no subject (0174), so the verdict moves from conditional to once. Hunted: a bare `move pool[k]` at an `OwningArray<T>` inside a loop (the required-`with` error, not loop-specific).

cells.rule: K3.12: "for move-only values ([§15.3](#sec-move-only-value-types)), any store into an owning location" | §15.3: "A **whole-value** move — a plain binding, a plain argument, a return — creates no such obligation on a **local**" | §15.1.1: "a `[N owned]T` slot is replaced, never taken: `move arr[i] with fresh`" | §15.3: "A whole-value `move` out of a **field** is the replacing `move` at the field (`var t := move h.Slots with fresh;`, [§28.8.1](#sec-the-replacing-move))" | §35.5: "the consumed binding is left **moved-from** when the construct completes" | §28.3: "A borrow of the consumed binding passed as an argument or operand evaluated **before** a consuming argument of the same call ([§22.5](#sec-optional-parameters-and-named-arguments)'s textual order) is such a borrow, its use being the call itself"
cells.note: Sub-shapes: unmarked assignment, plain passing and return move a move-only value (once); `case move c` routes payloads at selection (once); a slot of an owning inline array is exchanged — bare at `[N owned]T?` (stores `null`), `with` required at `[N owned]T` (the bare take rejected); a whole-value move out of a field is the replacing `move` at the field, leaving the replacement visible whole (once); `Sink(arr[0], arr)` is rejected by the #5750 sentence. The v0.334 inline-array slot window is retired (0174). Hunted: a borrowing-match binding over a field live across `move h.C with fresh` (a write point, §19.3: rejected); a whole-value field move whose `e` reads the field (reads the old value; the exchange follows).

cells.rule: §20: "When the branches are of a **move-only value type** ([§15.3](#sec-move-only-value-types)), a branch naming such a binding classifies by the **position the whole expression occupies**, exactly as a bare read of the binding does" | §20: "in an owned-consuming position — a binding, an assignment, a plain or `owned` argument, a `return`, an owning slot — the **selected** branch's value moves" | §20: "in a borrowing position — an operand, a receiver, an index — every branch is a borrow of its binding" | §20: "A move-only value is never bound by a borrow arm-meet: there is no copy for a borrow arm to protect" | §19.2: "an arm naming a move-only binding classifies by the position the `case` occupies"
cells.note: The v0.333 ambiguity (RC-D) is closed by the #5767 ruling. An if-expression branch, expression-`case` arm or `??` operand naming a move-only binding classifies by the whole expression's position. In an owned-consuming position the selected value moves (marker-free, the marker rejected) and the binding joins per-path consumed. In a borrowing position every branch is a borrow. The reassignment half (RC-E) is closed by #5768: a maybe-consumed move-only local takes a whole-value store that disposes per path. Statement joins follow K7. Hunted: `var y := (if c then a else b); case move y of …` (y owns the selected value; the other binding stays owned and auto-drops); a fresh-producer arm mixed with a binding arm in a borrowing position (a mixed meet, K7.3, or a temporary disposed at K8.1; sound either way).

cells.rule: K7.4: "owned ⊓ moved-from and owned ⊓ explicitly-disposed = **maybe-consumed** — unreadable after the join, no flow around a back edge into a use; scope-end disposal per-path" | §15.1.1: "A `[N owned]T?` slot takes bare — `move arr[i]` stores `null` — or with a replacement" | §28.3: "which is what makes the loop-carried spelling — `… Take(move r); … r := new Res(); end;` at the body's end — the ordinary way to carry an owned binding across iterations"
cells.cite: K7.4, §15.1.1, §15.3, §28.3 (State match on reassignment), §28.11, §29.2; proposal 0174; #5768
cells.note: Sub-shapes: a move-only local whole-value-moved inside a loop and declared outside it is maybe-consumed at the back edge (rejected without a reassignment, admitted with one); slot exchanges of an inline array per iteration hold `null` or the replacement afterwards (once); per-iteration move-only locals are auto-disposed per iteration. The v0.334 trackable-index and restoration legs have no subject (0174). No escape.

cells.rule: K3.8: "the operand of `throw` ([§31.1](#sec-the-throw-operand)) | none — the keyword announces | **moved-from** | **unfrozen** (K4.2, K5.3)† | after the matching catch arm completes, or at termination if uncaught" | §31.1: "the runtime's dispose-after-arm sets the disposed flag, so a borrow surviving the handler faults deterministically as `DisposedAccessException` in checked disposal mode" | §31.1: "Inside a catch arm, the bound exception variable (`var ex: Exception` in the arm pattern) is a **borrow** of the in-flight exception" | K3.2: "the task's result, [§30.5](#sec-result-lifetime-and-task-disposal)'s Pattern B transfer and Pattern A kind 1 (disposed by the awaiter or by the task's teardown, as §30.5 states)"
cells.note: Unchanged in substance. `throw x` transfers to the runtime: disposed after the matching arm, or at termination, and a surviving borrow is K4.1-backstopped. 0162 names the exception after its catch arm among the runtime's release points. A returned result transfers into the task's slot (K3.2), and a Pattern B await moves it out. A `catch` binding is a borrow. The 0168 retained-operand deferral (a re-raised fault instance) is C10's.

cells.rule: §28.3: "A *conditional* kill of any row joins to **maybe-consumed** ([K7.4](#sec-kernel-k7)) — one clause, applying to every row." | K7.4: "owned ⊓ moved-from and owned ⊓ explicitly-disposed = **maybe-consumed** — unreadable after the join, no flow around a back edge into a use; scope-end disposal per-path" | K3.5: "at the await, on all outgoing edges including fault and cancel"
cells.note: Unchanged. A task local awaited (Pattern B) or thrown on one branch joins maybe-consumed and is dropped per path. A `throw` arm absorbs.

cells.rule: K7.4: "owned ⊓ moved-from and owned ⊓ explicitly-disposed = **maybe-consumed** — unreadable after the join, no flow around a back edge into a use; scope-end disposal per-path" | §30.5: "A bind inside a loop body pins to the loop *body*: per-iteration disposal, no accumulation across iterations."
cells.note: Unchanged. A task declared outside a loop and Pattern-B-awaited inside it is maybe-consumed at the back edge (rejected, or admitted with a reassignment under #5768). Per-iteration tasks are disposed per iteration.

cells.rule: §29.8: "an iterable produced by an iterator method that declares an `owned` or move-only parameter ([§15.3](#sec-move-only-value-types)) — a parameter whose declared type is or contains a type parameter counting as move-only at every instantiation whose substitution makes that type move-only" | §29.8: "so `Each<T>(x: T)` mints a single-consumption iterable at `Each<Slot>` for an owning choice `Slot` and a re-iterable one at `Each<int>`" | §29.8: "the static check below applied at a call site that names such an instantiation, and the run-time check where a generic body's call substitutes its own type parameter" | K6.1: "an iterator frame minted over an `owned` or move-only parameter keeps the iterator frame's bound and is affine by the same rule" | K6.3: "callee-side, the unmarked mint-announcing return type transfers the container like an `owned` return"
cells.note: Closed (was ambiguous, #5800). The frame as an owned value transfers like an `owned` return (K6.3); an owned or move-only parameter transfers into the frame and on to the one enumerator; a parameter typed by a type parameter counts per instantiation (`Each<Slot>` single-consumption, `Each<int>` re-iterable), checked statically where the call names the instantiation and at run time inside a generic body. Sub-shapes: transfers once; a second consumption rejected or `InvalidOperationException`. No escape.

cells.rule: §29.7: "**in reverse order of establishment, exactly as if the body had exited at the suspension point**" | K7.4: "owned ⊓ moved-from and owned ⊓ explicitly-disposed = **maybe-consumed** — unreadable after the join, no flow around a back edge into a use; scope-end disposal per-path"
cells.note: Unchanged. Frame bodies use K7, and early disposal at a suspension point runs pending cleanups as if the body exited there, per path. A maybe-consumed frame-resident local is reassignable (#5768).

cells.rule: K7.4: "owned ⊓ moved-from and owned ⊓ explicitly-disposed = **maybe-consumed** — unreadable after the join, no flow around a back edge into a use; scope-end disposal per-path" | §29.7: "Runs the pending cleanup actions active at the point of suspension" | §29.2: "the iteration variable is either discharged by the program or auto-dropped with the warning"
cells.note: Unchanged in verdict. A loop around `yield return` uses R1's back-edge rule; abandonment mid-loop runs per-iteration cleanups. v0.334's 'a field or slot window may not contain a `yield return`' has no subject now: a replacing `move` may sit across a yield (0174). No escape.

cells.rule: K9.4: "static owned storage — a `static owned` field, and the slots of a `static readonly` owning inline array ([§22.12](#sec-static-members) note (h)) — admits no `move`, no slot store and no explicit disposal" | §22.12: "Its slots are fixed at initialization: a slot store or a `move arr[j]` through it is a compile error naming [K9.4](#sec-kernel-k9)" | §22.12: "it is the one admitted static of owning-inline-array type (a mutable one is rule 2's closing error)" | §22.13: "Static `owned` fields are disposed at program exit, after `Main` completes" | §28.6: "a `static owned` field read (a borrow of [K2](#sec-kernel-k2)'s always-live source, which only [§22.13](#sec-disposal-of-static-owned-fields)'s exit pass disposes — [K9.4](#sec-kernel-k9))"

What remains in R9 is decided. A `static owned readonly` field takes its one value from its initializer or the static constructor (the producer transfers into the field) and is disposed only by the exit pass. A `move` of it, an explicit `Dispose()` of it and any slot store or `move arr[j]` through a `static readonly` owning inline array are compile errors (K9.4, note (h)). A read is a borrow of the always-live source.

cells.rule: K9: "A field's obligation belongs to the object: it is discharged by the destructor cascade (owned fields, reverse declaration order) or by drop-on-overwrite, never by any scope's end" | K9.4: "static owned storage — a `static owned` field, and the slots of a `static readonly` owning inline array ([§22.12](#sec-static-members) note (h)) — admits no `move`, no slot store and no explicit disposal" | §22.12: "Its slots are fixed at initialization: a slot store or a `move arr[j]` through it is a compile error naming [K9.4](#sec-kernel-k9)" | App. C: "an assignment lexically inside a loop body in that window is rejected unconditionally"

A branch-dependent initializer is an R3 temporary meet. Reads are borrows of the always-live source.

Form (iv) is retired. A `static readonly` field's assignment inside a loop of its initialization window is rejected unconditionally, its slots are fixed (note (h)), and a `static owned` field admits no `move`. cells.rule: §28.1: "Such values carry no disposal obligation to transfer" | §28.9: "Capturing an *owned* class-typed local does **not** transfer ownership into the closure" | K1.6: "Values of runtime-managed type (`string`, `Type`, boxed value types, function values) and of ordinary value type carry no classification and no obligation"
cells.note: Unchanged. `owned` over a runtime-managed type is inadmissible or erased. Closure capture of an owned local is a borrow that the closure may not consume. Boxing a move-only value is rejected.

cells.rule: §28.9: "the closure may not assign to, transfer from, or dispose the captured binding, and may not outlive that scope" | K5.5: "and this is why a closure may not consume its captured owned bindings (K2 + decidability)"
cells.cite: K1.6, K5.5, K7.2, §28.3 (*Captured owned bindings*), §28.9

cells.rule: §28.9: "a closure cannot extend the lifetime of an owned class instance, so reclaiming the closure never leaves a destructor un-run" | §21.4: "The loop variable is freshly bound on each iteration: a lambda captured inside the body sees the value of that specific iteration."

cells.rule: K4.2: "**Site-announced kills.** A kill that is both **keyword-visible at the kill site** and **flag-backstopped** is **site-announced**, and is permitted while borrows of the value live: the announcement is the reader's notice and the flag is the safety net." | K1: "Scope-end machinery skips its disposal — the block is still freed at the holder's release point, [§28.2](#sec-checked-disposal)'s compiler-inserted free — and a straight-line read falls under [§28.2](#sec-checked-disposal)'s use-after-dispose warning regime rather than the moved-from error." | §28.2: "A *conditional* kill is treated more strictly: at a join of an explicitly-disposed path with a still-owned path the variable is **maybe-consumed** and a later use is a compile error" | §28.3: "An **explicitly-disposed** LHS requires an owned RHS too and displaces a **logically disposed** value: the store is that value's release point" | §28.3: "Locals that were already explicitly disposed before the throwing operation — the unwind disposes nothing for them and is still their release point, where the block is freed"
cells.cite: K1, K3.9, K4.1, K4.2, K5.3, K7.4, §28.2 (compiler-inserted free; use-after-dispose warning), §28.3 (State match on reassignment; Exception-path discharge), §28.6, §28.7, §17.13; #5832 (closed), #5759; #5830, #5810 (impl)
cells.note: Closed (was conflict, #5832). The kill (K3.9 call or discard) leaves the binding explicitly-disposed: §28.2's warning on every dominated use, consumes included; a maybe-consumed error after a conditional kill; surviving borrows K4.1-backstopped. Every path now frees the logically disposed block once at its holder's release point: the scope end (K1: the skip is the disposal's, not the free's), the overwrite (§28.3), or the unwind (the exception-path list now names it the release point). No escape.

cells.rule: §28.6: "requires a receiver the disposer **owns** (derives: [K3.9](#sec-kernel-k3)): an owned local or `owned` parameter, a `using var`, an unbound owned temporary ([§28.3](#sec-unbound-owned-temporaries)), a `move` result, or an `owned` field — or a slot of an owning inline array ([§15.1.1](#sec-owning-inline-arrays)) a field holds — read by code of the owning object's declaring type" | K1: "Scope-end machinery skips its disposal — the block is still freed at the holder's release point, [§28.2](#sec-checked-disposal)'s compiler-inserted free — and a straight-line read falls under [§28.2](#sec-checked-disposal)'s use-after-dispose warning regime rather than the moved-from error." | §28.10: "an explicit `Dispose()` of the source is permitted, and a read through the pinned binding afterwards raises `DisposedAccessException` in checked disposal mode" | A5: "`using var` is a scope pin: non-reassignable, never movable out" | §28.6: "`Dispose()` or a direct `DisposeAsync()` call through a **borrow** is a compile error." | §28.6: "the scope-end machinery of a `using var` or `await using var` whose `DisposeAsync()` was called directly skips it like any explicitly-disposed binding"
cells.cite: K3.9, K4.2, A5, §28.2, §28.6 (receiver list; K3.9 sentence), §28.10 (borrow-pin), §29.2 (`__source`), §30.5 (scoped await-bind slot); #5794, #5832 (closed); #4954, #4882 (impl)

A `using var` (or `await using var`) is an owned receiver: an explicit kill leaves it explicitly-disposed, its scope end skips the disposal and frees the block (K1 now says so), and A5 bars reassignment and move. A borrow-pin owns nothing; a site-announced kill of its source is flag-backstopped. No escape.

cells.rule: §28.6: "requires a receiver the disposer **owns** (derives: [K3.9](#sec-kernel-k3)): an owned local or `owned` parameter, a `using var`, an unbound owned temporary ([§28.3](#sec-unbound-owned-temporaries)), a `move` result, or an `owned` field — or a slot of an owning inline array ([§15.1.1](#sec-owning-inline-arrays)) a field holds — read by code of the owning object's declaring type" | §28.3: "an explicit `Dispose()` or direct `DisposeAsync()` on it is [K3.9](#sec-kernel-k3)'s consume, not a borrowing use, after which the boundary reclaims only ([§28.2](#sec-checked-disposal))." | §28.2: "An explicit `Dispose()` or direct `DisposeAsync()` ([§28.6](#sec-who-may-dispose)) performs **logical disposal only** — it sets the flag and runs the class's cleanup — and does not reclaim its receiver"

cells.note: Unchanged in verdict; the receiver list is re-quoted (#5794). `Make().Dispose()` is K3.9's consume and the K8 boundary reclaims only: one logical disposal at the call, one reclamation at the boundary; nothing can name the value afterwards. The discard `_ := Make();` disposes at the statement's end. No escape.

cells.rule: §28.6: "requires a receiver the disposer **owns** (derives: [K3.9](#sec-kernel-k3)): an owned local or `owned` parameter, a `using var`, an unbound owned temporary ([§28.3](#sec-unbound-owned-temporaries)), a `move` result, or an `owned` field — or a slot of an owning inline array ([§15.1.1](#sec-owning-inline-arrays)) a field holds — read by code of the owning object's declaring type" | §28.6: "The call is an **early release point**, not a discharge of the slot's obligation: the slot keeps its reference and its [K9](#sec-kernel-k9) obligation, and the containing object's teardown still runs the cascade over it ([§28.4](#sec-the-destructor) step 2)" | §28.6: "No replacement is owed: the call leaves the slot holding its disposed value, not a hole ([K9.2](#sec-kernel-k9))" | §28.6: "so the reader is [K4.1](#sec-kernel-k4)'s backstop: a member access through it raises `DisposedAccessException` in checked disposal mode and is undefined unchecked" | §28.7: "the store is the disposed block's release point, where [§28.2](#sec-checked-disposal)'s compiler-inserted free reclaims it"
cells.cite: K3.9, K4.1, K5.6, K9, K9.2, §28.2 (compiler-inserted free), §28.4, §28.6 (Who may call Dispose(); early release), §28.7; #5794, #5832 (closed); #5830 (impl)
cells.note: Unchanged in verdict; re-quoted (#5794's receiver wording). The declaring type's explicit `Dispose()` of an owned field (or of a field-held inline-array slot) is an early release, logical only; the slot keeps its reference and K9 obligation, the teardown's cascade (or a later overwrite, the release point by §28.7) issues the no-op and the single free. A later read is K4.1-backstopped. Hunted: dispose-then-`move _f with fresh` (the taker frees the disposed value at its release point; the field holds the replacement); dispose of another instance's field (declaring-type access). No escape.

cells.rule: §28.6: "and an element borrow of an **owning** collection (`pool[i].Dispose()` — use `Remove`/`RemoveAt`, the indexer-set, or `move coll[i]`, whose forms keep the slot state coherent" | §28.6: "(an element of an owning collection is a borrow, below)" | §28.11: "The compiler **must warn** when a local holding such a borrow is used (read, borrowed from, or passed) after a call on the **same collection binding** that **disposes the borrowed element** and **dominates the use on every path**" | K4.1: "**The backstop.** Disposal is idempotent and flag-setting; in checked disposal mode ([§28.2](#sec-checked-disposal)) any later use through any alias faults deterministically as `DisposedAccessException`, and unchecked mode is the same language with the check elided."
cells.cite: K3.1, K4.1, K4.2, K5.6, §28.3 (indexer row), §28.6, §28.11 (slot policy; use-after-removal warning; *`move` on a collection slot*), stdlib §4.5–§4.12, §4.21; #5794 (closed); #4777 (impl)
cells.note: `pool[i].Dispose()` on an owning collection is the borrow-receiver error; #5794 resolved v0.334's editorial seam (the owned-receiver list no longer names an owning-collection slot, and says an element of an owning collection is a borrow). Remove/RemoveAt/Clear/the indexer-set each dispose once; `move coll[i] with e` hands the element out with the slot refilled; a surviving element borrow is warned on the dominating same-binding shape and K4.1-backstopped otherwise; keyed removal is a recorded silence. Editorial residue noted (no verdict): §28.11's warning paragraph still cites 'the per-slot precision the moved-from tracking below uses', which 0174 deleted. No escape.

cells.rule: §35.9: "`Dispose` stays off the surface everywhere: choices do not implement `IDisposable`" | §17.13: "For a **move-only value** (an owning inline array `[N owned]T?`/`[N owned]T`, or an owning-classified choice) its owned slots — for a choice, the active case's owned payloads — are disposed in the usual order." | §17.13: "`x` is thereafter treated exactly as explicitly disposed" | §15.3: "A slot whose object was logically disposed earlier — by a discard of the value ([§17.13](#sec-the-discard-_)) or an explicit `Dispose()` of the slot ([§28.6](#sec-who-may-dispose)) — is live by that test: the pass's `Dispose()` is the no-op on its set flag and the store is the block's release point" | §28.6: "or a slot of an owning inline array held by an owned local or `owned` parameter of the body" | §9.4: "In checked disposal mode a read of the value in that state — through an in-place `this`, or through a borrowing-match binding of it, an owning inline array's slot reads, iteration and compiler-provided operations ([§15.1.2](#sec-members-and-operations)) included — faults as `DisposedAccessException`"
cells.cite: K3.9, K3.12, K4.1, §9.4, §15.1.1, §15.3 (Whole-value reassignment), §17.13, §28.2 (compiler-inserted free), §28.3 (State match on reassignment), §28.6 (receiver list), §28.7, §35.9; #5832, #5897 (closed)
cells.note: Closed (was conflict, #5832). Neither move-only kind has `Dispose()`; the explicit kills are the discard of a named binding (slots or active payloads disposed once, binding explicitly-disposed) and, since #5897, an explicit `Dispose()` of a slot of a local's owning inline array (§28.6). §15.3's per-slot pass now counts a slot whose object a discard or explicit slot `Dispose()` disposed as live, issuing the no-op `Dispose()` and freeing the block, so `_ := arr; arr := [...];` in a loop frees every slot object once. A destroyed holder's storage is §9.4's disposed state, flag-backstopped. No escape.

cells.rule: §31.1: "the runtime's dispose-after-arm sets the disposed flag, so a borrow surviving the handler faults deterministically as `DisposedAccessException` in checked disposal mode" | §31.1: "Inside a catch arm, the bound exception variable (`var ex: Exception` in the arm pattern) is a **borrow** of the in-flight exception" | K4.2: "and Pattern B `await` of an owned operand (a borrowed operand's award spends the task and kills nothing, [§30.5](#sec-result-lifetime-and-task-disposal))" | §30.5: "any await of an already-disposed task raises `InvalidOperationException`" | §30.9: "The exception is disposed **exactly once, by the task that owns it, at the later of the task's disposal and its settlement**"
cells.note: Unchanged in verdict; note re-worded for 0171 as the v0.335 lane asked. `throw x` and Pattern B `await` of an **owned** operand are the site-announced kills (K4.2's closed set now says so); a borrowed operand's award spends the task and kills nothing, its holder disposing it. Surviving borrows are flag-backstopped (dispose-after-arm; a task-owned fault disposed at the later of disposal and settlement). Hunted: dispose-then-await (`InvalidOperationException`); a second await of a spent borrowed operand (`InvalidOperationException`, §30.4).

cells.rule: §29.7: "a `MoveNext()` after disposal is an ordinary instance member access on a disposed instance and is governed by [§28.2](#sec-checked-disposal)" | §28.3 (Frame locals): "The site-announced kills of a carried borrow stay unfrozen under the flag: every read the frame makes through it is a member access" | §30.5: "any await of an already-disposed task raises `InvalidOperationException`" | §29.1: "a `Dispose()`/`DisposeAsync()` after an advance whose value was never taken **disposes the pending value**" | K6.4: "A **task's** are not traced by K5: their outlives-obligation is the K4.3-recorded settlement clause" | §30.5: "The task's own block stays live until that terminal state — its reclamation at the holder's release point is deferred there, never awaited or blocked on" | §29.8: "The first `GetEnumerator()` (or `GetAsyncEnumerator()`) transfers the frame's `owned` and move-only parameters to the enumerator it produces" | §29.8: "an iterable from which no enumerator was produced — its right never spent, or spent only by a transfer to a composed query or a callee that never enumerated it — disposes them itself when it is disposed"
cells.note: An explicit Dispose() of an enumerator or lazy-query frame runs §29.7's pending cleanup once and completes the machine; a later MoveNext() is a member access on a disposed instance (K4.1). An explicit Dispose() of an unsettled task attaches the result-disposing continuation and keeps the block live to the terminal state (0168); a later await raises InvalidOperationException. The untaken pending value is disposed with the enumerator. A site-announced kill of a carried source is unfrozen and flag-checked. The re-iterable `owned`-parameter route is now decided by proposal 0167 (route cell).

cells.rule: §28.6: "a `static owned` field read (a borrow of [K2](#sec-kernel-k2)'s always-live source, which only [§22.13](#sec-disposal-of-static-owned-fields)'s exit pass disposes — [K9.4](#sec-kernel-k9))" | K9.4: "static owned storage — a `static owned` field, and the slots of a `static readonly` owning inline array ([§22.12](#sec-static-members) note (h)) — admits no `move`, no slot store and no explicit disposal" | §22.12 (h): "Its slots are fixed at initialization: a slot store or a `move arr[j]` through it is a compile error naming [K9.4](#sec-kernel-k9)" | K2: "static storage — the one distinguished *always-live* source (process-lived, disposed only at exit, [§22.13](#sec-static-initialization-order));" | §28.3 (producers): "every admissible form keeps its referents alive to process exit" | §22.13: "Static `owned` fields are disposed at program exit, after `Main` completes"
cells.cite: K2, K9.4, §22.12 note (h), §22.13 (Disposal of static owned fields), §28.3 (Static field access row; Static stores), §28.6 (Who may call Dispose()); #5760, #5785, #5782 (closed); #5807 (impl)
cells.note: Closed by proposal 0162 item 4: a `static owned` field read is a borrow of K2's always-live source, so Dispose()/DisposeAsync() through it is the borrow-receiver error, and K9.4 bars explicit disposal (with `move` and slot stores) of all static owned storage, the `static readonly` owning-inline-array slots included; form (iv) is retired, so the mutable static owning inline array has no face here. The exit pass is the one discharger. Hunted at the narrowing's edges: the getter `Registry.M.Dispose()` (borrow error), `_ := _m;` (a borrow discard, cosmetic), `using var x := _m;` (a pin), passing `_m` to an `owned` parameter (borrow, rejected), a non-`owned` static holding a fresh value (non-owned field read, borrow error), element kills of a `static owned readonly OwningArray<T>` (Remove/Clear/indexer-set: R5 kills inside a referent, whose borrows are not static storage per *Static stores*, under rule 4's confinement warning).

cells.rule: K1.6: "Values of runtime-managed type (`string`, `Type`, boxed value types, function values) and of ordinary value type carry no classification and no obligation" | §28.3: "a closure cannot consume, reassign, or dispose a captured owned binding" | §8.6: "Move-only value types — owning inline arrays (`[N owned]T` and `[N owned]T?`) and owning-classified choices ([§35.4](#sec-choice-classification)) — cannot be boxed."
cells.cite: K1.6, §8.6, §28.1, §28.2 (summary: runtime-managed `Dispose()` is a no-op), §28.3 (Captured owned bindings), §28.9
cells.note: Runtime-managed values carry no classification or obligation, so an explicit `Dispose()` on one is the no-op and no use-after question arises. Hunted for an exemption leaking into an obligation path: a closure cannot dispose (or consume) a captured owned binding; a closure over a borrow of an owned local that is later explicitly disposed reaches the object only through member accesses, which K4.1 flags; move-only values cannot be boxed, so no box hides an owned slot from the kill.

cells.rule: §30.14: "the origin domain loses access **statically at the binding level** — the consumed binding is left moved-from, and the consume-site freeze ([§28.3](#sec-consume-site-freeze)) rejects the transfer while any local borrow of that binding is live" | §30.14: "class-typed arguments are `owned` and are moved through the spawn into the entry's parameter." | K4.3: "**Recorded trust, or nothing.** Where an admission's temporal guarantee can neither be statically compared (K2.3) nor flag-backstopped — the domain clause ([§28.3](#sec-borrow-lifetime-rules)'s field-store bullet, clause 4): a borrowed-from object transferred to, or made reachable from, another domain stays alive, so no flag is ever set" | §30.1: "the borrowed object must not be transferred to another domain"
cells.note: Unchanged. An owned binding crosses only as an `owned` spawn argument or channel `Send` (frozen); the origin binding is moved-from and the receiving domain discharges it; indirect pre-transfer aliases are the K4.3 domain clause, not flag-backstopped, named by the trust-admission report. Re-walked for 0174: a replacing `move box.f with fresh` into a spawn argument transfers the taken value and leaves `box.f` holding `fresh`, so the origin's field-held borrows of the old value are the same recorded domain clause. No escape.

cells.rule: A5: "`using var` is a scope pin: non-reassignable, never movable out" | §30.14: "the origin domain loses access **statically at the binding level** — the consumed binding is left moved-from, and the consume-site freeze ([§28.3](#sec-consume-site-freeze)) rejects the transfer while any local borrow of that binding is live" | §30.14: "class-typed arguments are `owned` and are moved through the spawn into the entry's parameter."
cells.note: A `using var` (and every compiler-introduced slot of its kind) is never movable out, and a class value crosses a domain only as an owned transfer, so the holder itself cannot reach another domain; its borrow-pin form owns nothing and a borrow is never sendable. What a scoped binding sends (`sender.Send(BuildReport(1))`, a `Clone()` of a pinned handle) is a fresh value, R3/C13.

cells.rule: §30.14: "class-typed arguments are `owned` and are moved through the spawn into the entry's parameter." | §30.15: "A send that **faults** disposes its class-typed item before the exception surfaces" | §30.15: "Disposing the `Channel<T>` itself closes it immediately and disposes every undelivered class-typed item in reverse insertion order"
cells.cite: K3.3, K8, §28.3 (Unbound owned temporaries), §28.8.1, §30.14, §30.15, stdlib §6.8, §6.9
cells.note: A fresh temporary passed to an `owned` spawn argument or `Send` transfers at call entry and is discharged on the receiving side; a faulting send disposes the item before the exception surfaces, a channel disposes undelivered items in reverse insertion order, and a temporary whose consuming call is never entered is disposed by the caller's unwind. Plain spawn rows admit no class type, so no temporary crosses as a borrow.

cells.rule: §30.14 rule 2: "an owning-inline-array field (`[N owned]C` / `[N owned]C?`) whose element class is a sendable class type" | §28.3 cl.4: "A field-stored borrow of an object later moved across a domain boundary — directly, or through a different binding such as `move box.f` into a spawn argument or channel send — is *not* rejected by the consume-site freeze below" | K4.3: "**Recorded trust, or nothing.** Where an admission's temporal guarantee can neither be statically compared (K2.3) nor flag-backstopped — the domain clause ([§28.3](#sec-borrow-lifetime-rules)'s field-store bullet, clause 4): a borrowed-from object transferred to, or made reachable from, another domain stays alive, so no flag is ever set" | K9.1: "stores the owned value `e` into the location and yields the displaced value, owned, in one step with no intermediate state"
cells.cite: K4.3, K5.6, K9.1, §28.3 (field-store cl.4), §28.4, §28.8.1, §30.14 (transfer-closed rule 2); proposal 0174
cells.note: Unchanged in verdict. An owned field crosses only inside its holder's owned transfer (every owned field sendable), so the receiving domain's teardown cascades over it once; a field `move` into a spawn argument or `Send` is now the replacing `move` (the field keeps its replacement, or `null` at a nullable field) plus an ordinary transfer. A borrow of the field's previous value left in the origin domain is the recorded domain clause. Editorial note (no verdict): §28.3 clause 4's example spells the bare `move box.f`, valid only at a nullable `f` under 0174.

cells.rule: §30.14: "an owning collection iff its element type is a sendable class type" | §30.14: "Moved-in items that were never processed are disposed by the runtime" | §30.15: "Disposing the `Channel<T>` itself closes it immediately and disposes every undelivered class-typed item in reverse insertion order"
cells.cite: §28.11, §30.14 (sendable statements; data-parallel combinators), §30.15, stdlib §4.5–§4.12, §6.9, §6.12; proposal 0174
cells.note: Unchanged in verdict. An owning collection crosses as one owned transfer iff its element type is sendable; a borrowing collection of class elements is not sendable (rejected); `Parallel.*` over `owned items` moves elements to workers and the runtime disposes unprocessed ones; a channel's buffered items are disposed once on its disposal. A slot taken by `move coll[i] with e` (0174) into a spawn is an ordinary transfer, the slot keeping its replacement; a borrow of the old element left behind is the R4 domain-clause shape.

cells.rule: §30.14: "**Value types** are sendable iff they are not borrow-bearing ([§9.7](#sec-records-and-disposal)), not move-only ([§15.3](#sec-move-only-value-types)), and **every component type is sendable**." | §30.14 rule 2: "an owning-inline-array field (`[N owned]C` / `[N owned]C?`) whose element class is a sendable class type" | §8.6: "Move-only value types — owning inline arrays (`[N owned]T` and `[N owned]T?`) and owning-classified choices ([§35.4](#sec-choice-classification)) — cannot be boxed."
cells.cite: §8.6, §15.3, §30.14 (value-type rule; transfer-closed rule 2), §35.12
cells.note: A move-only value is never sendable by itself (value-type rule) and cannot be boxed past the check, so a spawn argument, result or channel element of that type is rejected. As an owning-inline-array or owning-choice field of a sendable class it rides its holder's owned transfer and is disposed once by the receiving domain's cascade.

cells.rule: §30.14: "An exception that propagates out of the entry does not cross the boundary as an object" | §30.14: "The entry's task object never crosses the boundary: it lives and dies in the spawned domain" | §30.9: "The exception is disposed **exactly once, by the task that owns it, at the later of the task's disposal and its settlement**" | §30.15: "A send that **faults** disposes its class-typed item before the exception surfaces"
cells.note: No exception and no task object crosses: an entry's escaping exception is owned by the entry task in the spawned domain and disposed with it, while the join raises a fresh DomainFaultedException carrying copied strings; the join handle is an ordinary task of the spawning domain (Pattern B result transfer for `OwningTask<R>`). A pending `Receive` disposed before handoff gives the item back, and a faulting send disposes its item.

cells.rule: §30.14: "The entry's task object never crosses the boundary: it lives and dies in the spawned domain" | §30.1: "every borrow source reaching an async call must outlive the settlement of the returned task" | §28.3 cl.4: "A field-stored borrow of an object later moved across a domain boundary — directly, or through a different binding such as `move box.f` into a spawn argument or channel send — is *not* rejected by the consume-site freeze below" | K6.4: "A **task's** are not traced by K5: their outlives-obligation is the K4.3-recorded settlement clause"
cells.cite: K6, K6.4, K4.3, §28.3 (field-store cl.5), §30.1, §30.14 (Domain completion), stdlib §6.8
cells.note: Frames are interface- or Task-typed and never sendable, so no frame crosses; an `async` entry's task lives and dies in the spawned domain, and pending tasks left there continue under FireAndForget handling. A borrow a pending frame holds of an object later transferred to another domain is the §30.1 settlement clause's recorded domain extension (K4.3), not flag-backstopped.

cells.rule: §28.6: "a `static owned` field read (a borrow of [K2](#sec-kernel-k2)'s always-live source, which only [§22.13](#sec-disposal-of-static-owned-fields)'s exit pass disposes — [K9.4](#sec-kernel-k9))" | K9.4: "static owned storage — a `static owned` field, and the slots of a `static readonly` owning inline array ([§22.12](#sec-static-members) note (h)) — admits no `move`, no slot store and no explicit disposal" | K4.3: "No clause covers a **static-held** borrow, and none is needed" | §22.12 rule 4: "the referenced instance is reachable from every domain, and confining its use to one domain — or ensuring its own internal synchronization — is the programmer's obligation" | §22.12: "process-global storage of one is awarded once, to whichever domain's first await reaches it, and raises `InvalidOperationException` at every other"
cells.cite: K2, K4.3, K9.4, §22.12 (rule 4; note (j)), §22.13 (shutdown thread), §28.3 (Static stores), §28.6, §30.12; proposal 0171 (#5834, closed)
cells.note: Unchanged in verdict. No code disposes static owned storage before exit, and with 0171 the last in-place disposal of a static path (the Pattern B await) is gone, so K2's always-live claim holds on every path; the exit pass disposes once, alone on the shutdown thread. A kill inside a static's referent (an early field release, an element removal, a replacing `move` of its field) is rule 4's warned confinement obligation; a lock reached that way keeps §30.12's checked-mode detection (route). No escape.

cells.rule: §30.14: "**`string`** and **`Type`** are sendable; each crosses as a shared reference, which is safe because both are immutable" | §30.14: "**Function-typed values are never sendable**: their captures are borrows of the origin domain's scopes" | K1.6: "Values of runtime-managed type (`string`, `Type`, boxed value types, function values) and of ordinary value type carry no classification and no obligation"
cells.cite: K1.6, §28.9, §30.14 (string/Type bullet; function types; boxed values)
cells.note: `string` and `Type` cross as shared immutable references, a boxed value only if its type is sendable, and a function value never; none carries an obligation, so no cross-domain disposal question arises. Hunted: a function value smuggling captured owned bindings across (never sendable, and spawn entries are capture-free).

cells.rule: §28.6: "requires a receiver the disposer **owns** (derives: [K3.9](#sec-kernel-k3)): an owned local or `owned` parameter, a `using var`, an unbound owned temporary ([§28.3](#sec-unbound-owned-temporaries)), a `move` result, or an `owned` field — or a slot of an owning inline array ([§15.1.1](#sec-owning-inline-arrays)) a field holds — read by code of the owning object's declaring type" | K3.9: "logical disposal at the end of the discard statement ([§17.13](#sec-the-discard-_)) or at the call (for `DisposeAsync()`, completing at the returned task's terminal state, [§28.12](#sec-asynchronous-disposal)); reclamation at the holder's release point" | §28.12: "A second call to `Dispose()` or `DisposeAsync()` after either has **begun** is a no-op" | §28.2: "Where a direct `DisposeAsync()`'s task has not reached its terminal state at the holder's release point, reclamation is deferred to that terminal state: the release point neither awaits nor blocks" | §28.3: "(deferred, as there, to the terminal state of a direct `DisposeAsync()`'s task that has not reached it)"
cells.cite: K3.9, K4.2, K5.3, §28.2 (compiler-inserted free), §28.3 (State match on reassignment), §28.6, §28.12 (steps 1–2; second-call paragraph), §30.1; #5794, #5832 (closed); #5830, #5660 (impl)
cells.note: Unchanged in verdict; re-quoted (#5794). A direct `DisposeAsync()` on an owned binding begins logical disposal at the call and completes it at the task's terminal state; a second call in-window is the no-op with §28.2's warning; the block is released at the later of the holder's release point and the terminal state, never blocking — the overwrite of such a binding included (#5832: the store's free is deferred to that terminal state). Implicit discharge is synchronous. No escape.

cells.rule: §28.12: "**The `DisposeAsync` awaited is the run-time object's.**" | §28.12: "Over an owned right-hand side with no `DisposeAsync` to await — a value-type, runtime-managed or move-only right-hand side, or an object whose class does not implement `IAsyncDisposable` — scope exit takes the synchronous disposal (or the no-op) and likewise awaits nothing." | §30.7: "On **early abandonment** — the consumer disposes an iterator suspended at a `yield return` (one suspended at an internal `await` is [§29.7](#sec-disposal-of-partially-consumed-iterators)'s deferred disposal, whose cleanup awaits)" | §29.7: "so an `await using var` active there awaits its `DisposeAsync()`, as at every exit edge of an `async` body" | §28.6: "the scope-end machinery of a `using var` or `await using var` whose `DisposeAsync()` was called directly skips it like any explicitly-disposed binding"
cells.cite: A5, §28.6, §28.10, §28.12 (await using; run-time object; sync fallback), §29.7 (*Disposal while an advance is in flight*), §30.7; #5842 (closed); #5653, #5654 (impl)
cells.note: Unchanged in verdict; re-quoted (#5842's ruling scoped §30.7's fallback sentence to a `yield return` suspension). `await using var` awaits the run-time object's `DisposeAsync` on its normal and exception edges, disposes synchronously where nothing is to be awaited, takes the synchronous fallback on abandonment at a `yield return`, and — new at v0.335 — awaits its `DisposeAsync()` under the advance's continuation when the enumerator is disposed mid-advance (§29.7). A direct `DisposeAsync()` on the binding makes scope exit skip it. No escape.

cells.rule: §28.12: "**Implicit discharge is synchronous.** The implicit disposal paths — auto-drop of a plain-`var` owned local or undischarged `owned` parameter at scope end, the exception-path cleanup, drop-on-overwrite, container cascades, and frame teardown" | §28.3: "A temporary that is instead bound (to a `var`/`using var`), `move`d, returned, or transferred into an owning location is governed by the corresponding transfer or discharge rule and is **not** disposed under this rule (it would otherwise be disposed twice)." | §28.12: "the block is released then or at the holder's release point, whichever comes later — abandonment delays reclamation, it never skips it" | §28.3: "an explicit `Dispose()` or direct `DisposeAsync()` on it is [K3.9](#sec-kernel-k3)'s consume, not a borrowing use, after which the boundary reclaims only ([§28.2](#sec-checked-disposal))." | §28.3: "whose sources are the call's receiver and the sources its plain arguments contribute"
cells.cite: K8.1, K8.4, §28.3 (Unbound owned temporaries; Deferred-activation callees), §28.12 (Implicit discharge is synchronous; abandoned DisposeAsync task), §17.13, A6
cells.note: A temporary's boundary disposal is implicit and synchronous (the no-destructor warning covers the class side). `Make().DisposeAsync()` is K3.9's consume, after which the boundary reclaims only, and the release is deferred to the task's terminal state; the temporary is the frame's receiver source, so binding or storing the returned task past the full expression is rejected by the deferred-activation rule, and awaiting it in place is once. An abandoned DisposeAsync task still runs to its terminal state; 'abandonment delays reclamation, it never skips it'.

Decided legs: the advanced-but-untaken element is disposed by the enumerator; drain views hand items out; element overwrite during iteration is an element-level write; abandonment passes the collection's disposal. A slot exchanged in the body holds `null` or its replacement (0174), so the frame's pass meets live values and nulls only; an iterator member on a move-only receiver is rejected. No escape.
