routes.rule: §28.6: "in the body of a `DisposeAsync` override itself, not in a lambda nested in it, `base.DisposeAsync()` is [§28.12](#sec-asynchronous-disposal) step 2's chain, not a disposal of `this`, and is admitted" | §28.12: "an override that does not chain forgoes that level's asynchronous cleanup, and its destructor body is skipped all the same" | §28.12: "an override's chained `base.DisposeAsync()` is not such a call but a step of the logical disposal already under way, and triggers no reclamation of its own" | §28.12: "owned fields are disposed in reverse declaration order and the base class's reclamation chains, once, immediately after logical disposal has completed, whichever path ran" | §28.12: "An instance is **logically disposed** — the state [§28.2](#sec-checked-disposal)'s checked-mode test faults on — once its logical disposal has completed"
routes.note: A `DisposeAsync` override's `base.DisposeAsync()` is a step of the logical disposal already under way and triggers no reclamation; its accesses are the disposal's own and run on a live instance. Not chaining forgoes the base level's async cleanup by statement; chaining twice re-runs user code only, since the owned-field cascade and chain run once, immediately after logical disposal completes. No language-managed obligation is doubled or leaked.

routes.route: A15 self-returning enumerator: a loop's enumerator disposal logically disposes a borrowed receiver its owner still holds
routes.rule: A15: "the disposal of a self-returned frame runs `Dispose()` without reclaiming" | §29.1: "The disposal of a self-returned frame therefore **runs the object's `Dispose()` and does not reclaim it**" | §29.1: "so the object is reclaimed exactly once however many times its enumerator face is taken and disposed — including when the receiver is a borrow the caller does not own" | K4.1: "in checked disposal mode ([§28.2](#sec-checked-disposal)) any later use through any alias faults deterministically as `DisposedAccessException`"
routes.note: Unchanged at v0.334. A `for` over a borrowed self-returning enumerator logically disposes the owner's object at loop end, reclaim left to the owner (A15); the destructor runs once, and the owner's later use faults under K4.1. Proposal 0162's 'explicit disposal marks, the holder frees' generalizes A15's non-reclaiming disposal, so the block is live when the owner's later use tests the flag.

routes.route: §30.11 completion-source carve: task object owned by the source; late completion and source disposal
routes.rule: §30.11: "**Task-object ownership.** The **source owns the task object** its `Task` property exposes." | §30.11: "an await through the borrow spends the task and disposes nothing, per [§30.5](#sec-result-lifetime-and-task-disposal)'s borrowed-operand rule, and the source's own later disposal of it is the task's single disposal, finding no result" | §30.11: "For either kind, a **never-awaited** task is disposed exactly once, by the source at source disposal." | §30.11: "A source disposed before completion first faults the task (below) and then disposes it"
routes.note: Unchanged in verdict; re-quoted for 0171's alignment: an await of an `OwningTaskCompletionSource<T>`'s task through the borrow spends it and disposes nothing, and the source's disposal is the task's single disposal (the v0.334 accounting, where the await disposed and the source's call was the idempotent no-op, is gone). Never-awaited tasks are disposed by the source; a source disposed before completion faults then disposes. Once.

routes.route: async enumerator disposed while a `MoveNextAsync()` advance is in flight (frame suspended at an `await`, not at a `yield return`)
routes.rule: §29.7: "Such a disposal neither waits nor raises: it begins the enumerator's logical disposal ([§28.12](#sec-asynchronous-disposal)) and returns at once (`DisposeAsync()` with a completed task), and the frame's disposal is **deferred to the pending advance's settlement**." | §29.7: "When the awaited operand settles the body does not resume and the suspended `await` awards nothing" | §29.7: "the machine is completed, and the advance's `Task<bool>` settles with `false`, or faults with the exception a cleanup action raised" | §29.7: "and the receiver and borrowed parameters the frame holds stay under [§30.1](#sec-async-methods)'s settlement obligation until then" | §29.7: "the frame, the cleanup actions active at the suspension point and the enumerator's block are held to process exit"
routes.cite: §29.7 (*Disposal while an advance is in flight*), §30.1, §30.5, §30.7, §28.12, K4.3; #5842, #5891 (closed); #5900 (impl)
routes.note: Decided (was missing) by #5842's ruling and #5891's clarification: the disposal returns at once; at the advance's settlement the body does not resume, the operand's product is disposed with an owned operand (or left to a borrowed operand's holder), the active cleanups run under the advance's continuation (an `await using var` awaiting its `DisposeAsync()`), the frame's parameters follow, the advance settles `false`, and the block is reclaimed then. The receiver and borrowed parameters ride §30.1's settlement clause (K4.3). An operand that never settles holds the frame to exit, a recorded liveness posture. In the v0.334 counterexample `closed` prints once, after the 50 ms delay.

routes.route: destructor body's bare take of a non-nullable owned field, then a read of the emptied field through another spelling (a call on `this` in the same body, or a base class's destructor reading an inherited field)
routes.rule: K9.3: "a destructor body may take a field of the object it tears down bare — `move x.f` with no replacement, whatever the field's nullability: teardown reads it no more and the cascade skips the emptied field" | §28.8.1: "at a non-nullable field the field holds no value for the rest of the body — a later read of it there through the field's own spelling is a read of a moved-from location ([K1](#sec-kernel-k1)) and is rejected until the field is reassigned" | §28.8.1: "The exemption reaches only the fields of the object the destructor tears down" | §28.4: "Destructors run in subclass-to-base order."
routes.cite: K1 state 3, K9.2, K9.3, §28.4, §28.8.1 (*Constructors and destructors*), §13 (`protected`), App. C.3; #5913 (open)
routes.note: Opened (pre-existing, newly exposed): 0174 made 'no location ever holds a hole' the invariant and set aside only the destructor's bare take, whose later read is rejected 'through the field's own spelling' only. Face 1 (#5913's): a call on `this` later in the same destructor body reads the emptied non-nullable field through another method's spelling. Face 2 (not in #5913): a derived destructor takes an inherited `protected owned` field bare — 'the fields of the object the destructor tears down' does not say 'declared by its class' — and the base destructor, which runs after it, reads the field through its own spelling in another body. Either read meets `null` typed non-null: no disposed object, so no K4.1 flag and no K4.3 clause. #5913's readings 1–2 are confined to one body and do not reach face 2.

routes.route: the replacing `move loc with e` as a transfer: order of the receiver, index, replacement and checks; a holder consumed, overwritten or resized inside `e`; a borrowed receiver
routes.rule: §28.8.1: "evaluates `loc`'s receiver and index, then `e`, and then, **in one step with no intermediate state**, stores `e`'s value into the location and yields the location's previous value, owned" | §28.8.1: "so a consume of the holder binding inside `e` is frozen as at a call's receiver ([K5](#sec-kernel-k5) clause 5)" | §28.8.1: "so nothing `e` does (a call that resizes the collection or empties the field, a suspension at an `await`) can invalidate them" | §28.8.1: "A borrow of the displaced value taken before the exchange is bounded afterwards by the taker, under the posture every field or slot overwrite already has" | §28.8.1: "a borrowed parameter included, as v0.332 ruled for the take ([#5695](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5695)); the holder keeps its invariant whatever the receiver's own classification, and the taker owns what left" | K4.1: "in checked disposal mode ([§28.2](#sec-checked-disposal)) any later use through any alias faults deterministically as `DisposedAccessException`"
routes.cite: K3.1, K4.1, K5 clause 5, K5.6, K9.1, K9.5, §28.2, §28.3 (Unbound owned temporaries), §28.7, §28.8.1 (*The replacing `move`*), §28.11, §22.3 (`ref`/`out` locations); proposal 0174 (#5923); #5695
routes.note: New route for the replacing `move` (v0.336). Hunted: (1) a holder binding consumed inside `e` (`move p._r with Make(move p)`, `move arr[0] with F(arr)` at a move-only local) — frozen, rejected; a `ref` rebind of an owned holder — already barred by §22.3's owned-state bound; (2) a field holder overwritten inside `e` (`move _pool[0] with Rebuild()` where `Rebuild` runs `_pool := …`) — the receiver evaluated first is a borrow of the old collection, which the overwrite disposed; the bounds check after `e` touches it, so checked mode faults (K4.1, fields not frozen, K5.6) and the produced replacement is the unwind's unbound temporary; unchecked it is the backstop's undefined behavior, as for any argument borrow a later argument invalidates; (3) a resize inside `e` — checked after `e`; (4) a borrowed receiver — the overwrite posture. Once-backstopped.

routes.route: an exception inside the replacing `move`: a throwing receiver, index or replacement, a failed bounds/key/`!` check, or a fault at the exchange
routes.rule: §28.8.1: "An exception raised while evaluating the receiver, the index or the replacement, or by one of those checks — an out-of-range index, a `KeyNotFoundException` at an absent dictionary key, `NullReferenceException` under `!` at a location holding `null`, a throwing constructor in `e` — leaves the location unchanged" | §28.8.1: "a replacement already produced is an unbound owned temporary disposed by the unwind" | §28.8.1: "The exchange itself runs no user code and disposes nothing" | §28.3: "When the full expression is instead exited by an **exception** — an operand or argument evaluated later throws before the temporary's transfer or consumption point — every already-produced, not-yet-consumed unbound owned temporary is disposed during unwinding"
routes.cite: K3.15, K8.1, K9.5, §28.3 (Unbound owned temporaries), §28.8.1 (*The replacing `move`*), §28.11; proposal 0174 (#5923)
routes.note: New route for the replacing `move` (v0.336). Every raise inside the form leaves the location holding its old value and disposes an already-produced replacement once in the unwind; the exchange runs no user code, so no destructor can raise between take and store. A checked-mode fault at the exchange itself (a receiver disposed during `e`) is not in §28.8.1's list but is a raise before the replacement's transfer point, so §28.3's unbound-temporary rule disposes it. Once.

routes.route: drop-on-overwrite whose displaced disposer throws: the store is abandoned at a location the overwrite was the release point of — what does the location hold once the raise is caught (an instance field, an owning slot, a local whose scope encloses the handler)?
routes.rule: §28.7: "a throwing disposer during overwrite propagates after the store is abandoned, leaving the new value an unbound owned temporary" | §28.2: "the overwrite for a displaced value ([§28.7](#sec-reassigning-owned-fields))" | §28.4: "Before it propagates, the **remaining steps of the generated `Dispose()` still run**: the remaining owned-field disposals (reverse declaration order) and the base-class chain complete, and physical reclamation still occurs" | §28.7: "Every slot the pass disposed is left empty — an unobservable state, reached only on the abandoned store's unwind, where the displaced value's only remaining reader is the unwinding discharge itself" | K9.2: "a non-nullable owned field or owning slot holds a live value at every instant" | App. C.3: "no owned location is ever observed holding a hole, by any alias, callee, continuation or destructor, in either build mode"
routes.cite: K3.11, K4.1, K9.2, K9.5, §28.2 (The compiler-inserted free), §28.4 (*Destructors should not throw*), §28.7 (*Ordering and exceptions*), §15.1.1, §15.3, §28.11 (indexer-set), stdlib §4.5 (setter sketch), App. C.3; proposals 0162, 0174; #4490 (impl)
routes.note: New at this run (pre-existing since v0.334's 0162 made the overwrite the displaced value's release point; the inline-array face newly contradicts v0.336's K9.2 and C.3). §28.7 abandons the store when the displaced value's disposer throws, while the free at that release point still reclaims (§28.4). Nothing says what the location then holds. Class-typed field, local or owning slot (the stdlib setter is `_storage[i] := value`): reading 1, it keeps the reference to the reclaimed block, so a caller that catches the raise reads freed memory (no live flag) and the location's own release point frees the block a second time; reading 2, it is emptied, a hole at a non-nullable location; reading 3, the reclamation waits for the location's next release point (the explicit-disposal posture, §28.6), so later reads fault on the flag and the block is freed once. Owning inline array: §28.7 states reading 2 ('left empty') and calls it unobservable because only the unwind reads it — false for an instance field, or for a local whose `try` sits inside its scope, against K9.2 and C.3.
